sections.h2: Twelve states burn nearly three-quarters of India's petroleum products

chart.title: Gujarat is the largest fuel market, ahead of more populous Maharashtra

chart.source: PPAC, Statewise Sales of Petroleum Products workbook.

sections.means: The twelve largest state markets account for 73.1% of national sales, so state policy covers most of the demand.
sections.todo: Read state-level fuel policy against these twelve markets first, since they carry nearly three-quarters of the total.

sections.h2: Petrol sales grew +255% nationally, against +77% for diesel

sections.means: The diesel-to-petrol ratio fell from 4.6 to 2.3, because the increment is two-wheelers and cars rather than trucks.
sections.todo: Focus diesel-to-CNG conversion on Haryana and Rajasthan, the high-ratio states with the most diesel left to convert.

sections.h2: Odisha's fuel sales nearly tripled; Delhi's grew only 22%

chart.title: The fastest growth sits in the eastern mineral belt, while Delhi plateaued

sections.means: Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand lead growth, driven by late motorisation on top of mining and industrial freight.
sections.todo: Plan for motorisation in the eastern mining belt, where fuel demand is still compounding fastest.
